Bug_Title: Child class methods named for parent class methods should be overrides
Bug_Explanation: The Child class has methods named for parent class methods (doSomething and doSomethingElse) that do not properly override the parent methods. The first bug is that the Child's doSomething method is not an override because it uses a different type of Pear (from the Fruit class) than the Parent's doSomething method (which uses a Pear from the Computer class). The second bug is that the Child's doSomethingElse method is not an override because the Parent's doSomethingElse method is static, which means the Child's method cannot hide it.
Seed_Compilation_Fail_Details:
../sonar_clean_java_code/result_Sonar_126/seed_Sonar_126.java:35: error: doSomethingElse() in Child cannot override doSomethingElse() in Parent
    public void doSomethingElse() { // Bug: this is not an override of the static parent method
                ^
  overridden method is static
1 error
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered when the Child's doSomething method is called with a Fruit.Pear object. This is not an override of the parent method because it uses a different type of Pear (from the Fruit class) than the Parent's doSomething method (which uses a Pear from the Computer class). Also, the Child's doSomethingElse method is called which is not an override of the static parent method.
